stories.title: Halys Makes History — Maiden ATP Title in Kitzbühel
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Quentin Halys (FRA, 29) defeated defending champion Alexander Bublik (KAZ, No. 1 seed) 6-4, 7-6(6) in the Generali Open Kitzbühel final on Saturday July 25 to claim his first career ATP title. The win ended a 14-year professional journey — Halys earned his first ATP ranking point in 2012 at age 15. He became the first Frenchman to win the Kitzbühel title in the Open Era (France was 0-6 in previous Kitzbühel finals). Halys fired 17 aces and never faced a break point in the match (1h33m). He rises 32 places to No. 51 in the ATP Rankings (career high was No. 46). Bublik's bid for the first Kitzbühel title defense since 2013 came up short.

stories.title: Estoril Final — Van Assche vs. Blockx (All-Unseeded ATP 250 Decider)
stories.angle: NEW STORY — The Millennium Estoril Open (ATP 250, clay) reaches its final today (Sunday July 26) with an unprecedented all-unseeded matchup: Luca Van Assche (FRA, No. 78) vs. Alexander Blockx (BEL). Van Assche stunned top seed Rublev in the QF ("biggest win of my career") then beat Hugo Gaston 6-4, 7-5 in an all-French SF. Blockx pulled off one of the week's great comebacks in his SF: trailed Darderi 5-7, 0-5 in the third set before reeling off seven consecutive games to win 5-7, 7-6(1), 7-6(5). Quote from Blockx: "I have no words." Both players are competing in their first ATP 250 final. Final at 3:00 PM local (10:00 AM ET).

stories.title: WTA Hamburg Final — Bondar vs. Korpatsch; Sherif Retires in SF
stories.angle: NEW STORY — The MSC Hamburg Ladies Open (WTA 500, clay) final is today (Sunday July 26): Anna Bondar (HUN) vs. Tamara Korpatsch (GER, wildcard). The semifinal results brought a twist: Mayar Sherif (EGY), who had dominated the week including a 6-2, 6-3 QF demolition of Badosa, retired against Korpatsch at 6-1, 2-0 with an injury after accumulating a heavy clay-court load. Korpatsch advances to her first WTA 500 final on home clay. In the other SF, Bondar outlasted Elina Avanesyan 7-6(3), 4-6, 7-6(2) in a 3h29m marathon. Korpatsch is a German wildcard competing in a hometown Hamburg final.

stories.title: WTA Prague Final — 18-Year-Old Tagger Upsets Krejcikova, Into First WTA Final
stories.angle: NEW STORY — The Livesport Prague Open (WTA 250, clay) final is also today (Sunday July 26): Daria Snigur (UKR, No. 8 seed) vs. Lilli Tagger (AUT, 18, unseeded). Tagger — currently ranked No. 90 — pulled off the week's biggest upset Friday, defeating Barbora Krejcikova (CZE, No. 2 seed, two-time Grand Slam champion) 6-7(5), 6-3, 7-6(4) in 2h50m, coming back from a set down. Tagger, from Lienz, Austria, trained at the Francesca Schiavone Academy in Varese and won the 2025 French Open girls' title. Snigur (UKR) beat Valentova 7-6(4), 6-2 in the other SF.

stories.title: Clay Season Finale — Hard Court Pivot Begins This Week
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Today marks the end of the European clay season. Four tournaments — Kitzbühel (ATP 250), Estoril (ATP 250), Hamburg (WTA 500), and Prague (WTA 250) — all close today, with the last clay champions crowned before the North American hard-court swing. The Canadian Open / National Bank Open (women's Toronto Aug 1–11; men's Montreal Aug 4–13) is the immediate next stop. With Sinner (elbow), Djokovic (injury), Alcaraz (injury), Draper (arm), and Paolini (foot) all absent from their respective draws, Alexander Zverev and Ben Shelton (defending champion) headline the men's field in Montreal. The Canadian Open draws are expected July 29–30.
